request.query: Register as a resident and get a Finnish personal identity code (DVV)

sources.title: dvv.fi
highlights: You can get a personal identity code if you are residing legally in Finland and there are grounds for registration, such as
a certificate of registration of the right of residence for EU citizens
Everyone who requests a personal identity code must visit in person within 1 month of submitting the form, including children
a valid passport or an official photo ID card of a citizen from an EU member country, Iceland, Norway, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, or San Marino
proof of work or studies in Finland, for example, a certificate of student status or an employment contract (employee, check your right to work
Finnish identity code request (work, study) 2–3 weeks
Book an appointment to the service "Registration of a foreigner´s personal data

sources.title: lomakkeet.dvv.fi
highlights: You will receive a Finnish personal identity code when you register

sources.title: finlandhandbook.com
highlights: If you submit your request in August or early September, expect the DVV processing times to stretch toward the 4-to-6-week mark
You might find that the first available slot for identity verification is three weeks away, and only after that does the 1–3 week processing clock begin
If you see no appointments in Helsinki, widen your search radius
If the clerk has everything they need in one go, your application can be processed in the "fast track" queue

sources.title: nordicexpat.com
highlights: Book as early as you can; if slots are scarce, check service points in nearby municipalities and the booking system at different times of day

sources.title: helloexpat.eu
highlights: Staying under a year and expecting a municipality of residence
